known_failures.note: Bugs seen while reading the test documents. Each was found after the test run and left unfixed: fixing it there would turn the test set into a development set. The next pass fixes these on the development split and re-measures once.
rule_decisions: Only top-level breakdown items count as grading gold. Four emitted sub-weights on PHYS S102E ('written test' 15, 'oral test' 5, 'online section discussion' 10, 'participation' 10) are statements the document does make inside a parent category, so they are scored as misses by that rule. Counting them correct would make precision 55/68 = 0.809 instead of 51/68 = 0.750; the pre-registered rule is what the report quotes.

failures.note: The extracted office-hours value is the *next* section's body ('Class: Thursday E1-E3 ... Screening: Wednesday ...'), not the section the evidence span points at ('Office Hours: Wednesday periods 9-11').
Office-hours body is the course overview text that follows the heading, so 'By appointment' never appears in the value. Emitted at confidence 1.000.
Office-hours body is the instructor/email block that follows, not 'Schedule via email'. Emitted at confidence 1.000.
The document states only 'Office Hours: TBD', which is not an office hour; the body is emitted anyway (with the next bullet glued on), at confidence 1.000.
Same shape: 'Office Hours of Professor: TBD' is emitted as a value, glued to the email line.
The instructor's office number 'MAT 328' is emitted as the course code, at confidence 0.991; the document's actual code is printed on an adjacent line as 'Course Code: ECO 3704'.
The meeting room 'CRR 0521' is emitted as a course code, at confidence 0.982.
The room 'FLO 100' is emitted as a course code; here the confidence (0.002) at least admits it is a guess.
The parenthetical '(25% lowest, 35% best)' is split into category fragments 'lowest' and 'best)' at confidence 0.996, and 'Extra Credit 0-1%' becomes the category 'Extra Credit 0'.

Nested sub-weights are flattened into top-level categories: 'written test' 15%, 'oral test' 5%, 'online section discussion' 10%, 'participation' 10%. The values are printed in the document, but a reader summing the categories now gets more than 100%.
'General Information' — a section heading that occurs verbatim in the document — is returned as the title at confidence 0.995.
